AuthConfig.description: An auth config, without its secret.

has_secret_settings.description: Whether the app has secret settings (which are never answered).

settings.description: The provider's own settings for the app; an empty object when it has none.

basehead.description: `base...head`, each a branch, a tag or a commit SHA; `owner:branch` names another fork's.

per_page.description: At most 100; pages the commits between them.

credential_kind.description:
What the connection acts as: `oauth` (the user who consented) or `app_installation` (an
installation of the auth config's app, its tokens minted when an action runs). An open
string.

installation_id.description: The installation an `app_installation` connection acts as.

last_error.description: Why the last refresh or the consent failed.

refresh_task.description: The pending refresh task's name, and when it runs.

setup_complete.description:
Whether setup is complete: osiris holds the tokens and, when they can be refreshed, their
refresh is scheduled. When false, the connection can't be used.

status.description:
`pending` (the consent is open), `active`, `disabled` (no refresh is scheduled, so the
connection can't be used: after a failed connect the user must connect again; after a
refresh, osiris schedules it again by itself), `expired` (the provider refused a refresh
or the grant is gone: reconnect) or `failed` (the consent failed or was never finished). A
connection is only reported `active` when its setup is complete.

redirect_url.description:
The provider's own consent page: send the browser here. Absent for an installation
connection, which needs no consent.

secret_settings.description:
The provider's own secret settings for the app, never answered. A GitHub app that acts as
its installations puts its App's private key here: `{"private_key": "-----BEGIN …"}`.

settings.description:
The provider's own settings for the app, which it validates; answered back. A GitHub app
that acts as its installations names its App id here: `{"app_id": "12345"}`.

path.description: The file to comment on, relative to the repository's root.

position.description: The line of the file's diff to comment on, from 1.

alias.description: Yours: a mark for this attempt, to find what it made if its answer is lost.

auth_config_id.description: `ac_…`: the provider's app to connect through.

callback_url.description:
Where the browser goes after the provider's consent, with `connected_account_id` and
`status` added to its query. Required for a consent; left out with `installation_id`.

installation_id.description:
Connect as this installation of the auth config's app instead of through a user's
consent (a GitHub App's installation id): no browser, active at once. The auth config
must hold the app's credentials in its settings.

user_id.description: Yours: who the connection is for, such as an organization's id.

branch.description: The branch to commit to; the default branch when left out.

content.description:
The file's new content as text. Ignored when `content_base64` is given; an empty file when
both are left out.

content_base64.description: The file's new content, base64-encoded, for a binary file.

sha.description: The SHA of the file being replaced; required to update an existing file.

ref.description: The full reference, starting with `refs/`, such as `refs/heads/feature`.

auto_init.description: Whether GitHub makes a first commit with an empty README.

gitignore_template.description: The name of a `.gitignore` template GitHub offers, such as `Rust`.

homepage.description: A URL with more about the repository.

license_template.description: The keyword of a license GitHub offers, such as `mit`.

branch.description: The branch to commit to; the default branch when left out.

sha.description: The SHA of the file being deleted.

ref.description: The reference without `refs/`, such as `heads/feature` or `tags/v1.0.0`.

owner.description: The account or organization that owns it.

code.description:
`OS_00` unauthorized, `OS_01` not found, `OS_02` invalid request, `OS_03` conflict,
`OS_04` provider refused, `OS_05` provider unavailable, `OS_06` connection not active,
`OS_07` unknown version, `OS_08` idempotency key reused, `OS_09` request in flight,
`OS_10` body too large, `OS_11` missing scopes, `OS_99` internal. An open string: codes may
be added.

EventDelivery.description:
An event as a subscriber receives it on the events topic, written in the instance's pinned
release. The type and the connection's id, never its data: fetch the connection for its state.

Fields may be added without a new release, so a subscriber ignores one it doesn't know.

event_id.description: `ev_…`, the same each time the event is delivered, so a client can drop repeats.

osiris_version.description: The API release the event is written in, also the message's `osiris_version` attribute.

type.description:
What happened, also the message's `type` attribute: `connection.active`,
`connection.expired` or `connection.revoked` today. An open string: new types may come
without a new release, and a client ignores a type it doesn't know.

organization.description: The organization to fork into; the authenticated user's account when left out.
